8.translation:
Search supports circular-origin binding; set ⟦shared:0⟧ for a linear sequence.
The actual pUC19 hits shown here should be inspected in the returned table. Search hits are computational matches, not experimental validation.
Primer ⟦shared:1⟧ mode finds an exact suffix, with no mismatch model;
its Wallace melting-temperature estimate is a composition heuristic.

12.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ supports curated exact-reference annotations, DNA and
record-specific matching modes. Protein searches use standard-code six-frame
translation; they do not implement splicing, alternative initiation or
origin-crossing protein matches. Source genetic-code metadata does not select
another translation table. For nonstandard codes use DNA matching or external
code-aware analysis. Confidence is a heuristic label, not a probability.
Use [explicit CDS projection](⟦shared:1⟧) for known protein/genome maps.

14.translation:
This short workflow uses the same source-backed plasmid as the complete map. The [complete pUC19
workflow](⟦shared:0⟧) demonstrates catalogue annotations, exact reference
matching, site display filtering, primer labels and feature stacking together.
Changing only a sequence name does not make it a recognized reference; sequence
content determines source-backed recognition. Read the result methods and
methylation provenance instead of assigning reference claims to an unknown sample.

16.translation: Inspect match positions, methods and provenance. Restriction filtering is a display choice; methylation search conditions are not a measurement of an unknown sample.

18.translation: After inspecting matches, follow [primer arcs and text](⟦shared:0⟧) and [restriction labels/leaders](⟦shared:1⟧). See [circular layers](⟦shared:2⟧) for backbones/centre/lanes and [circular labels](⟦shared:3⟧) for fixed/automatic text.

19.translation: ## A catalogue is not a search result ⟦shared:0⟧

20.translation: `primer_catalog` returns oligonucleotide records; aliases=TRUE returns source aliases. Catalogue direction is descriptive; find_primer_bindings determines binding direction on target DNA. Multiple names for one sequence do not represent distinct oligonucleotides. Continue with [primers](⟦shared:0⟧) to search and draw.
